articles.title: Everton drop Jack Grealish from Carabao Cup tie over ‘breach of club discipline’
articles.summary: England player left out of squad to face Newcastle. Moyes confirms he ‘supports’ the club decision. Jack Grealish was dropped from Everton’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle following a breach of club discipline.
body: Everton took the unusual step of announcing that Grealish’s omission from the fourth-round tie was for disciplinary reasons on social media, after listing David Moyes’s team for the fourth-round tie at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The club posted on X: “Jarrad Branthwaite remains sidelined for a second successive game due to concussion protocols, while Jack Grealish is unavailable for selection due to a breach of club discipline.”
It is understood the 31-year-old missed training on Monday without permission and the decision to drop him was taken by Moyes in conjunction with the Everton chief executive Angus Kinnear.
Speaking after Everton’s 3-1 win, Moyes said: “I’m not going to give any details. It was a club decision and I support it. I don’t want to speak too much about it.”

Grealish returned to training at Everton’s Finch Farm complex after Monday’s absence but is expected to be fined for his unauthorised absence earlier in the week. The playmaker had missed Everton’s defeat at Arsenal on Saturday due to illness.

articles.title: George Russell determined not to let disappointing F1 season define career
articles.summary: 28-year-old still believes he will win world title one day. Kimi Antonelli misses media duties with ‘viral illness’ George Russell has insisted he will not let his difficult Formula One season define his career and believes he still has plenty of years left to come back and win the world…
body: Russell has been outdriven by his 20-year-old Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli in a bruising season for the British driver. Antonelli is set to win the title and become F1’s youngest world champion at this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix if he finishes in ninth place or above.

He has taken nine wins thus far to Russell’s three, with the British driver struggling for consistency in adapting to the demands of the energy management required by the new cars which, alongside the tyres in use this year, does not suit the 28-year-old’s driving style.

Russell has delivered some impeccable weekends, including commanding victories in Austria and Baku, but more often than not has been left baffled as to why he cannot make the car work to the same effect as Antonelli, a process which he conceded had been hard to deal with.

“I’ve probably learned more about myself this year than I would have liked to, in all honesty,” he said at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez. “You know, the highs and lows you go through in sport are immense and that’s because we all care so much for what we’re doing.

articles.title: Everton ease past Newcastle to set up Fleetwood trip after Grealish is dropped
articles.summary: The biggest night in Everton’s season started with a big call from David Moyes and demanded a big performance from his players. With the exception of Jack Grealish, they did not let him down.
body: Newcastle dominated spells of the fourth round tie and the stats – registering 28 shots to Everton’s 11, although only nine visiting attempts were on target – but individual defensive errors and an ineffective attack proved a ruinous combination. Matthias Jaissle denied his team are a soft touch, despite persuasive evidence to the contrary, yet called Newcastle “naive” and the defeat, in front of almost 8,000 of their fans, “shocking”. Andy Burnham was among the many Evertonians in attendance grateful for Newcastle’s generosity.

James Garner, with his first goal of the season, Hayden Hackney, with his first goal for the club, and Thierno Barry were on target to take Everton into the last eight of a competition they have never won. Jordan Pickford was in commanding form against his old adversaries while Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall ran the show from midfield. But it was the absent Grealish who dominated the buildup after Everton announced he had been dropped for disciplinary reasons.

articles.title: PSG claim late point after Shaw penalty to hit Manchester City’s WCL top-four hopes
articles.summary: You cannot miss half a dozen big chances at Women’s Champions League level and expect to get away with it. That is the harsh lesson Manchester City learnt on Thursday against Paris Saint-Germain, who extended the English champions’ wait for their first win in Europe this season by striking late to…
body: City’s third draw from three Champions League games so far this season really ought to have been a victory. Instead, their hopes of a top-four spot and with it automatic qualification for the quarter-finals are looking increasingly slim.

They thought they had won the game through Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s 85th-minute penalty, but conceding sparked PSG into life and they snatched a point with a scrappy equaliser three minutes later as their substitute Tara Elimbi Gilbert found the net from close range.

How, therefore, should we look upon City’s season? Are they the team that is unbeaten in all competitions? Or the team without a win in Europe? Both ring true, and although they are still likely to progress to the knockout stages, they will have been hugely frustrated with their profligacy.

articles.title: Ireland's Furlong cleared of groin grab by disciplinary committee
articles.summary: Ireland's Tadhg Furlong is cleared by a disciplinary committee of grabbing Gavin Coombes in the groin during Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster.
body: Munster back row Coombes raised the allegation with match referee Andrew Brace in the first half of Leinster's 24-18 win at Aviva Stadium, but television match official (TMO) Colin Stanley could not find conclusive video evidence.

However, three-time British and Irish Lions tourist Furlong was subsequently cited over an act of foul play under Law 9.27, which says "a player must not do anything that is against the spirit of good sportsmanship including but not limited to grabbing, twisting or squeezing the genitals".

The disciplinary panel, comprised of Simon Thomas (Wales), Attie Heyns (South Africa) and Pamela Woodman (Scotland) met on Thursday and "unanimously concluded the citing complaint against the player should be dismissed, on the basis that he did not commit an act of foul play contrary to Law 9.27".
While they dismissed the complaint, the disciplinary committee concluded Coombes had given "an honest account of his recollection of events surrounding the incident".

articles.title: Russell: 2026 F1 season won't break me
articles.summary: George Russell insists this year's Formula 1 season "won't break me" as Kimi Antonelli is set to become world champion this weekend in Mexico.
body: A top nine finish for Antonelli, or Russell or Lewis Hamilton failing to win Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix, would secure the title for the Italian, who would be the youngest champion in F1 history at 20 years old.
Russell came into 2026 as favourite after dominating Antonelli last year but has won just three races to his team-mate's nine, regularly being outperformed throughout the season.

"I've probably learned more about myself this year than I would have liked to in all honesty. The highs and lows you go through in sport are immense. That's because we all care so much for what we're doing," said Russell.
"I remind myself I'm 28 years old. I see Lewis still competing extremely well at 41 and Fernando at 44. Lewis won the majority of his titles in his 30s.

articles.title: Run, fly, repeat: A Utah woman prepares for 7 marathons in 7 days on 7 continents
articles.summary: Utahn Melissa Walker plans to run seven marathons on seven continents in one week, recovering on a chartered plane between races — with chocolate chip cookies and Coke.
body: Walker signed up for The Great World Race, a fledgling test of endurance in which runners hopscotch the globe in a chartered plane to run 26.2 miles in Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia. There are no hotels or spas. They’ll eat, sleep and recover on the plane between continents.
Even Walker, a 50-year-old married mother of four, admits it’s beyond crazy.

Irish physician and former international runner David Kelly founded The Great World Race in 2024, drawing on his experience supporting endurance events in Antarctica and the North Pole to organize seven marathons on seven continents in seven days.

“Who it’s for: Those who desire an adventure that’s seldom found in our modern world, have the training, time and resources to embark on the most ambitious marathon on earth,” according to its website. And it’s not cheap, coming in at about $55,200 per runner.

articles.title: Buccaneers’ Emeka Egbuka among players included in latest injury report before Falcons game
articles.summary: Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is showing signs of progress in his recovery, although his status for Sunday’s Week 8 clash with the Atlanta Falcons remains up in the air.
body: Buccaneers’ Emeka Egbuka among players included in latest injury report before Falcons game appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Egbuka was a limited participant in Thursday’s practice as he continued to work through the NFL’s concussion protocol. One encouraging sign was his return to a regular practice jersey after previously wearing a non-contact one. The development suggests he is making progress, though he still needs medical clearance before returning to game action.

The rookie has been out since sustaining a concussion and a foot injury in the Buccaneers’ Week 6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. During the fourth quarter, Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen delivered a hit that brought his shoulder into Egbuka’s helmet as the receiver tried to make a play on an incomplete pass. The injuries forced him to sit out Tampa Bay’s Week 7 win over the Carolina Panthers.

His return would give the Buccaneers another important option in their passing game. Before going down, Egbuka had caught 28 passes for 240 yards and two touchdowns, making him a productive contributor to the team’s receiving corps.

articles.title: Former IVC, now Purdue volleyball star Kenna Wollard, shares cancer diagnosis, update
articles.summary: Kenna Wollard has come forward about the illness that has kept her sidelined this college volleyball season. The Purdue volleyball all-American revealed via social media on Thursday, Oct. 29 she was diagnosed with Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma in August.
body: "Today, I found out that the treatments are working and I am on track to remission!!!!" she posted. "These past couple months have been so tough but hearing the news today brought so much joy. I still have some treatments left, but I am very hopeful for what’s ahead."

Wollard played in the program's initial 2026 exhibition but hadn't appeared in any of Purdue's matches during her senior season. She was a Big Ten All-Conference first-team selection and second-team All-American in 2025.
"I never would have thought I would be spending my senior year this way," she wrote. "But I do believe everything happens for a reason and this is Gods way of making me a stronger, better person.

"I’m so grateful for how well I’ve responded to everything and for the outcome I am expecting. The love and support I’ve received has made this journey 1000000x better. I truly am SO loved. These pictures are just a snapshot of how blessed I am. I can’t wait to share another update when I’m done with treatment and back to my normal life."

articles.title: 'Lack of talent' - Alonso doubles down on Albon criticism
articles.summary: Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso has doubled down on his criticism of "low level" Formula 1 drivers who have a "lack of talent" following his collision with Williams' Alex Albon in Austin.
body: Albon tried to overtake Alonso for 12th place into the Turn 11 hairpin on the opening lap of the United States Grand Prix, but went into the side of the Aston Martin driver, damaging both cars.
Neither driver received a penalty and both were able to continue with Alonso finishing 16th and Albon in 17th in Austin.

Post-race, Alonso stated the quality of the drivers in the bottom third of F1's grid is "very low" and he had not changed his stance in Thursday's media day ahead of this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix.
"I think it's simply a very low level of driving and lack of talent," he told Sky Sports F1.

articles.title: 'I'm built differently' - Hamilton defiant over extending F1 career into 2030s
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton insisted he "is built differently" as he continued to rule out extending his Formula 1 career into the 2030s.
body: Following the announcement earlier in October that Africa will return to the F1 calendar at some point in the 2030s with a race in Rwanda, Hamilton had said he hoped he would be able to compete in the first grand prix on the continent since 1993.

Given Hamilton turns 42 in January and will be 45 at the start of the 2030 F1 season, at which point it is far from certain the circuit in Rwanda will be ready, it was initially unclear how seriously his comments should be taken.

But quizzed on the topic on Thursday ahead of this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, the seven-time world champion said: "I mean, firstly, you've never had anyone like me here in the 70 years [of the sport's history], so I feel that I'm built differently.

"Of course, there are challenges up ahead that I can't foresee that come with age. But along this way, along this journey, there have been so many preconceived ideas about the fact that your reaction time drops off.
